result:
The world is a vast, unpredictable canvas of experiences, and every day feels like a new brushstroke. This morning, I woke up to the sound of rain tapping against my window—gentle at first, then insistent, as if the sky had something urgent to say. I brewed a cup of coffee, the steam curling into the cool air, and watched the droplets race down the glass. There’s something deeply comforting in the rhythm of rain, a reminder that even chaos has a melody.

I’ve been thinking a lot about time lately—how it slips through our fingers like sand, how we chase it, hoard it, waste it, and yet it never stays. A year ago, I was in a different city, surrounded by different faces, convinced I had everything figured out. Now, I’m here, in this quiet moment, realizing how little I actually knew. Growth isn’t linear; it’s a spiral, circling back to the same questions but with new eyes.

I’ve also been reading about the ocean—how it covers 71% of the Earth’s surface, how it’s home to creatures we’ve barely begun to understand. The deep sea is a mystery, a world of bioluminescent wonders and pressures that would crush us instantly. It’s humbling to think about how much we don’t know, how much we’ll never know. Maybe that’s the beauty of it—the endless unknown, the thrill of discovery, the quiet awe of standing at the edge of something vast and uncharted.

Life, like the rain, like the ocean, is a constant motion. And for now, that’s enough.
